page: Amazon Web Services m3.large is a general-purpose, third-generation server instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor. This dedicated CPU configuration provides 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the hardware belongs to an older generation with limited processing capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1301.38 falls into the bottom 25%, while the multi-core score of 1706.78 is in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show poor throughput, with read-only large block transfers at 14.03 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 12.02 GB/sec. Geekbench metrics further confirm these limitations, yielding a single-core score of 693.0 and a multi-core score of 802.0.

Given the poor performance across CPU, memory, and database operation benchmarks, this instance presents significant performance tradeoffs compared to modern hardware. However, the inclusion of 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast local disk access relative to its processing tier. The server is suited for legacy general-purpose workloads, basic web serving with a static web serving throughput of 1.95 GB/sec, lightweight background utilities, or low-demand development and testing environments that do not require high computational density.
